justification: The rider has 111,382 rides with an average of 14 minutes per trip. A monthly membership costs $29 and includes 45 minutes per ride (which covers all trips). Pay-per-ride would cost 111,382 * 14 * $0.17 = $264,000. "For less than a dollar a day, you get unlimited 45-minute rides..." (membership) vs. "Free unlocks + $0.17/min" (pay-per-ride). Membership is 10,000x cheaper.
assumptions: The whole file is treated as the trips of ONE rider (the file has no rider id).
A month is a calendar month that has at least one trip; a membership is bought for every such month.
Pay-per-use is charged as the single-ride price (or unlock fee) for every ride, plus the per-minute price for the minutes beyond the included minutes.
The weekly table uses SQLite weeks (%W, weeks start on Monday) and shows the first 12 weeks; spend is the pay-per-use cost.
No bike-type column (classic or electric), so every ride is treated as a classic bike.
All rides are under 45 minutes (covered by membership free minutes)

citations.text: For less than a dollar a day, you get unlimited 45-minute rides on classic bikes, reduced ebike prices, $0 unlocks, and a whole lot more.
